concern: The security case rests on the 500 response body leaking a traceback with absolute media paths. If aiohttp/HomeAssistantView returns a generic '500 Internal Server Error' body and logs the traceback server-side only, the leakage half of the argument is false and the idea shrinks to log noise plus a wrong status code.

The mismatch is only a live defect if coordinator.readings is actually populated from status.hub_readings and the storage repair path is reachable at runtime. Nobody traced readings from producer to _storage; if another writer supplies un-suffixed keys, the repair works and the fix would break it.

The repair may be the second surfacing, not the only one. sensor.py already exposes storage_used_percent as an entity a user can automate or badge on, and coordinator.py:631 feeds a storage trend from it. If the percent sensor already tells the user the hub is filling up, fixing the dead repair adds a redundant notification rather than restoring a lost warning, and the impact case collapses to tidiness.

The fan-out premise behind both offline-8's severity and its DA attack is unshown: nobody has verified that a media-browser listing actually issues N concurrent preview requests. preview.py's own header notes the card marks images loading="lazy", which would serialize or suppress most of them, and Home Assistant's browse response may return thumbnails without fetching them at all. If previews arrive one at a time on scroll, there is no pile-up through the lock and the unbounded-hold scenario needs a different trigger.

Nobody has shown the session can actually hold the lock unboundedly. If the client's socket or HTTP layer already carries a read timeout, a wedged handshake raises on its own and the lock releases without any new code — the whole idea then reduces to shortening an existing timeout. The api.py connect/read path and its timeout arguments need opening before the bound is priced.

The '60s empty card' half of the severity case looks false: _load()'s finally clears _busy and calls _render() when the in-flight request returns, so a click swallowed by the _busy guard leaves the card empty only until that response lands. If so, the residual symptom is a seconds-long stale label, and the request-token rewrite is bought for less than claimed.
